from: sovereign desk (operator 'תמשיך' — continue the rungs: shim-side retry/backoff queue was CR-0022's booked next-rung)
proposes: zai-openai-shim v1.1.0 — bounded retry/backoff queue on TRANSIENT upstream failures, implementing the exact next-rung CR-0022 booked ('shim-side retry/backoff queue'; their measured trigger: z-ai 429 killed graft's whole-repo synthesis while consumers correctly ate the fail-loud 502). Contract-compatible upgrade: same endpoints, same response shapes, same 502 {error:{type:'upstream_error'}} on FINAL failure. Mechanics: (1) transient classifier is textual (the SDK throws messages, not statuses): 429/rate-limit/quota/too-many/timeout/ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT/EAI_AGAIN/5xx/bad-gateway/overloaded; (2) bounded queue: SHIM_RETRY_ATTEMPTS (default 3 total attempts), exponential backoff SHIM_RETRY_BASE_MS..SHIM_RETRY_CAP_MS (default 400..2000ms, capped, in-memory only, no fs); (3) retries complete BEFORE any byte returns (upstream call is internally non-stream even for SSE) so backoff only delays first byte — SSE consumers safe; (4) SHIM_SELFTEST_429=1 arms a ONE-SHOT simulated 429 (default off, consumed on first use) so the retry path is live-fire provable without waiting for a real upstream 429; (5) /health gains additive retry fields (consumers match status/service — additive is safe); (6) SHIM_PORT env for parallel self-test instances (default 3040 unchanged); (7) new log line family: upstream_retry attempt=N/M backoff=Xms model=... — the final-failure line is byte-identical to v1.0.1's. Tier B law untouched: no keys, no bash, no fs.
rationale: CR-0022 measured the gap: a single z-ai 429 zeroes a multi-call consumer task (graft deep synthesis died mid-flight). The queue converts one-blip-loses-the-task into bounded resilience while preserving the fail-loud law — after the queue exhausts, the consumer still gets the same honest 502. The self-test hook keeps the fleet's proof culture: the retry path is demonstrated by receipt, not by hope.
risk: Low. Bounded total added latency ≤2.4s (400+800+~capped) per request worst case; no unbounded waits; no state beyond in-memory counters; one-shot selftest flag cannot fire twice. The live :3040 instance runs v1.0.1 and was NOT restarted by this CR (not ours to kill) — v1.1.0 activates on the next natural shim start (run-with-shim.sh edge guarantees per-run freshness), documented here so no one expects the running health to flip mid-flight. Textual classifier can in principle retry a non-transient error whose message happens to match (e.g. a 500-shaped app error) — bounded by attempts, harmless by volume.
verdict: PASS — live-fire receipts on a parallel instance (SHIM_PORT=3041, live 3040 untouched): (A) /health → version 1.1.0, retry {attempts:3, base_ms:400, cap_ms:2000, selftest_armed:true}; (B) SELFTEST 429 flow: chat request → simulated 429 on attempt 1 → 'upstream_retry attempt=1/3 backoff=400ms ... 429 rate limited (SHIM_SELFTEST_429 one-shot)' in the log → attempt 2 real call → 200 with correct content, end-to-end latency 784ms (400ms backoff + ~384ms real call); (C) one-shot consumption: second chat request → zero retry lines, 200 'DIRECT-OK'; (D) final-failure path code-identical to v1.0.1 (unchanged catch + 502 shape); (E) test instance stopped after receipts, live instance still v1.0.1 at health check.
judged_by: live-fire receipts (health JSON, retry log line with exact backoff, 200 responses with correct content, one-shot consumption proof) + code-diff review of the unchanged failure path
